strings.title: The Deadly Rehearsal
strings.hint: The stage pistol is supposed to be harmless… who replaced the blank with a live round? Trace who entered the props room alone.
strings.solvedText:
The culprit: theater props master Rami Fouad.

The actor had discovered that Rami was stealing and selling the theater's antique possessions and threatened to expose him after the performance. Rami, the only person controlling the scene's pistol, replaced the blank cartridge with a live round before the onstage shooting scene. The actor died before the audience in what appeared to be a "rehearsal accident." Rami then tried to put the empty cartridge back, but it was too late.

Live-ammunition gunpowder residue in his props drawer, his solo entry into the weapons room before the show, and the victim's messages threatening to expose his thefts proved his guilt.
strings.summary.text: During a play's opening performance, the lead actor fell bleeding after a shooting scene supposedly performed with a blank-firing pistol. The audience thought it was brilliant acting, until he did not get up. The bullet was real. Backstage access was restricted, and only a handful of people controlled the stage weapon.

strings.scene.address: National Theater — the stage and props room
strings.scene.intro: A scene pistol meant to be loaded only with blanks. The props room holds the weapon and theatrical ammunition under one person's supervision. The access log shows a solo visit an hour and a half before the show.
strings.scene.notes[0]: A live round replaced a blank in the scene pistol
strings.scene.notes[1]: One person manages the props room
strings.scene.notes[2]: Solo entry into the weapons room at 19:40
strings.scene.notes[3]: The victim threatened to expose thefts of theater possessions
strings.evidence[0].title: The Scene Pistol
strings.evidence[0].desc: Loaded with a live round instead of a blank. Its design allows the substitution by someone familiar with it.
strings.evidence[1].title: Props Drawer
strings.evidence[1].desc: Live-ammunition gunpowder residue in the props master's drawer, where it does not belong among blanks.
strings.evidence[2].title: Weapons Room Log
strings.evidence[2].desc: Rami Fouad entered alone at 19:40. He was the last person to handle the weapon before the performance.
strings.evidence[3].title: Threatening Messages
strings.evidence[3].desc: The victim's messages to Rami: "I know which theater possessions you're selling. I'll tell management after the show."
strings.evidence[4].title: Theater Inventory Record
strings.evidence[4].desc: Antiques disappeared from the theater storeroom over a year, the latest a week ago.
strings.suspects[0].name: Fadi, the Director
strings.suspects[0].relation: An artistic dispute with the victim
strings.suspects[0].alibi: "I was in the control room running the show in front of the crew."
strings.suspects[0].statement: Tarek and I disagreed over his performance, an artistic disagreement like any production has. His death destroyed my play and my reputation. I never go near the weapons. They are solely the props department's responsibility.
strings.suspects[1].name: Rana, the Understudy
strings.suspects[1].relation: Aspires to play his wife onstage
strings.suspects[1].alibi: "I was changing in my room during the scene."
strings.suspects[1].statement: Yes, I aspire to bigger roles, as every actor does. But my colleague's death in front of me was a shock, not an opportunity. I know nothing about weapons and have never entered the props room.
strings.suspects[2].name: Rami Fouad
strings.suspects[2].job: Props master and stage weapons supervisor
strings.suspects[2].alibi: "I loaded the pistol with blanks as usual and handed it over. I don't know how it became a live round."
strings.suspects[2].statement: I've worked at this theater for fifteen years. The actors' safety is my sacred responsibility. I loaded blanks as I do every night. Tarek's accusations about the inventory were a misunderstanding I was going to explain. Whoever switched the round wanted to destroy me as well as Tarek.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Stage Assistant
strings.witnesses[0].statement: I saw Rami enter the weapons room alone before the show and close the door. That was unusual: inspections always take place with two people present.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Lighting technician
strings.witnesses[1].statement: The shot was louder and sharper than on every rehearsal night. I knew immediately that something was different, but it was too late.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Theater Storekeeper
strings.witnesses[2].statement: Tarek came to me a few days earlier asking about missing items. He said he suspected a crew member of selling them. He gave no name, but seemed certain.
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Shooting Report
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body: A fatal gunshot injury during a theatrical performance was reported. The theater was cordoned off and the crew prevented from leaving.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic medicine
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Gunshot Report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body: A live pistol round. The range matches the stage scene. Death was almost immediate.
strings.folders[2].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Pistol Examination
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body: The weapon was designed for blanks but had been loaded with a live round. The substitution required precise knowledge of its mechanism.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Props Drawer Examination
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body: Live-ammunition gunpowder residue was found in the supervisor's drawer, with no legitimate explanation for its presence.
strings.folders[3].name: Interviews
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Rami Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body: His solo entry and the gunpowder residue are critical. He evaded questions about the missing antiques.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Director Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body: His presence in the control room is documented. He has no connection to the weapons.
strings.folders[3].docs[2].title: Understudy Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[2].body: The dressing-room corridor camera documents her changing clothes.
strings.folders[4].name: Confidential files
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: Inventory Sales Record
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: An online sales account under an alias belongs to Rami. The missing theater items were sold through it.
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Confession Record
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body: Confronted with the gunpowder and sales record, he confessed: "He was going to destroy my life with a word… I wanted to silence him, not for him to die like this."
strings.reports[0].title: Weapon Report
strings.reports[0].author: Evidence team
strings.reports[0].body: Replacing a blank with a live round required solo access and knowledge of the mechanism. Only the props master fits both.
strings.reports[1].title: Motive Report
strings.reports[1].author: Assigned investigator
strings.reports[1].body: The victim's threat to expose thefts of theater possessions provides a direct motive for the only person controlling the weapon.
strings.notes[0].text: Who can replace a blank with a live round? Someone who knows the weapon.
strings.notes[1].text: The victim was about to expose the inventory thief
